importance_ranking.reason: Extreme visual variation across sub-types — single FRP cabin, GI multi-seat block, mobile toilet van, handicap unit — buyers use the image to identify product type before reading any text. Wrong sub-type shown = immediate skip regardless of specs or price.

No. of seats, wall material, and toilet seat type (Indian/Western) are non-negotiable shortlisting criteria — a 1-seat FRP cabin and a 10-seat GI block cannot substitute for each other. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated by contractors or government procurement officers.

Price varies dramatically across spec tiers (single FRP cabin vs 10-seat GI block vs bio-digester unit) and buyers on IndiaMART discover and compare across tiers. Indian B2B buyers — especially construction contractors and government agencies — are price-aggressive and use listed price as a primary shortlisting signal after spec confirmation.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Recognised brands exist with buyer recall — Tata Nestin/EzyNest and Sintex Sugam are specified by name in institutional and government procurement; sibling MCAT 'Sintex Portable Toilets' (182628) confirms brand-driven search behaviour in this category.
importance_ranking.reason: Manufacturer track record, installation capability, and after-sales service matter to institutional buyers (municipal corporations, government agencies, EPC contractors) during vendor selection. Brand names are referenced in government tender specifications.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Multi-seater blocks are quoted per block/per set; mobile toilet vans per vehicle — but in all cases the unit is entirely implied by the product type and never a buyer question. No price comparison confusion arises.
importance_ranking.reason: Modular toilets are discrete manufactured units — per piece is the only conceivable unit for a single cabin. No buyer would question whether a toilet cabin is sold per piece.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Seat count defines the entire product class — a 1-seat cabin and a 10-seat block are non-interchangeable and carry dramatically different prices; no buyer can substitute one for the other.

FRP, GI/MS, PUF panel, and RCC represent distinct durability and price tiers — non-interchangeable across project requirements — with significant price deltas between lightweight FRP and heavy-duty RCC or PUF-insulated GI construction.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Government tenders and site planners specify required footprint (e.g., 4x4 ft, 6x4 ft) — sellers need this to confirm they can supply the required size and for buyers to plan installation space.

Bio-digester (DRDO zero-discharge) vs septic tank connection vs holding tank are non-interchangeable for sites without sewage infrastructure — a primary compliance and site-suitability criterion for government and highway deployments.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Indian vs Western WC configuration is non-interchangeable — sellers who manufacture only one type cannot supply the other, making this the primary routing spec for accurate seller response.
Material defines the durability tier and price range — FRP specialists and GI/steel fabricators are different supplier types, so this spec determines which sellers can accurately quote and supply.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Seat count is the primary sizing parameter — a contractor needing a 10-seat labour camp block and one needing a single cabin are entirely different procurement requirements, and sellers need this to determine which product range to quote.
